title: Manchow Soup
description: Manchow Soup is a popular Indo-Chinese restaurant-style soup packed with finely chopped vegetables, aromatic garlic, ginger, green chilies, soy sauce, and chili sauce. A lightly thickened savory broth is finished with spring onions, crispy fried garlic, and crunchy fried noodles for the signature contrast of textures and flavors.

ingredients.title: For the Soup Base
items: Bell peppers – ½ cup, finely chopped
Spring onions – 3–4, white and green parts separated

ingredients.title: For the Fried Noodle Garnish
items: Thin crispy fried noodles – ½ cup

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Vegetables
steps: Finely chop and slice all vegetables into small, uniform pieces.
Keep the mushrooms and cabbage prepared separately for easy addition during stir-frying.
Separate the white and green portions of the spring onions.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Building the Soup Base
steps: Heat 1–2 tbsp oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add chopped garlic, ginger, green chilies, and the white parts of the spring onions.
Sauté briefly until aromatic without allowing the garlic to brown.
Add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent.
Add carrots, cabbage, bell peppers, and mushrooms.
Stir-fry for 2–3 minutes, keeping the vegetables slightly crisp.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Adding the Broth & Seasoning
steps: Pour the vegetable or chicken stock into the wok.
Add soy sauce, chili sauce, black pepper, and salt.
Bring the soup to a gentle boil and allow the flavors to combine.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Thickening the Soup
steps: In a small bowl, mix the cornstarch with 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Slowly pour the slurry into the boiling soup while stirring continuously.
Cook briefly until the soup reaches a lightly thickened, silky consistency.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Preparing Crispy Garlic
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a small pan over medium heat.
Add the sliced garlic and fry until evenly golden.
Remove immediately and drain once crisp to prevent the garlic from burning.

instruction.title: Step 6 – Finishing the Soup
steps: Add the green parts of the spring onions to the soup.
Taste and adjust the soy sauce, chili sauce, salt, or black pepper as needed.
Keep the soup hot until ready to serve.

instruction.title: Step 7 – Restaurant-Style Serving
steps: Ladle the hot soup into serving bowls.
Top generously with crispy fried noodles and fried garlic.
Sprinkle with additional black pepper for extra aroma.
Serve immediately while the garnish remains crisp.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve piping hot as an Indo-Chinese appetizer.
Top with crispy fried noodles immediately before serving for maximum crunch.
Pair with vegetable fried rice, Hakka noodles, chili chicken, or other Indo-Chinese dishes.
Serve in warm bowls to maintain the soup's temperature.

chefTips: Keep the vegetables slightly crunchy; overcooking will make the soup lose its characteristic texture.
Use a flavorful homemade stock instead of water whenever possible for greater depth.
Build the aroma by sautéing garlic, ginger, chilies, and spring onion whites before adding the vegetables.
Add the cornstarch slurry gradually so the soup becomes silky and lightly thickened rather than gummy.
Fry the garlic carefully and remove it as soon as it turns golden, as it continues cooking briefly after removal.
Add crispy noodles only at the time of serving so they retain their texture.
For a spicier restaurant-style version, replace or supplement the chili sauce with Schezwan sauce.
